caseno: Criminal petition for Special Leave to Appeal Nos. 77 & 78 of 1975.
lawyer:
Dr. Aleem-Al-Razee, Advocate with Abu Taher Chowdhury, Advocate, Supreme Court, instructed by S.M. Huq, Advocate-on-Record (absent) ----- For the Petitioner.
Not represented ----- For the Respondents.
parties:
Haider Ali ----- Petitioner.
Vs
Bangladesh and others ----- Respondents.
full_judgment:
Kemaluddin Hussain, J.- The two petitions are heard analogously and disposed of by one order as a common question of law is involved. The question is whether under regulation 3(2) of Martial Law Regulation No. 1 of 1975, the Court of Special Judge set up under the provision of Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 (Act. XL of 1958) is a Criminal Court. The High Court Division held it to be so. These orders are under challenge in these Special Leave Petitions. 

 2. Two cases under section 409/34 of the Penal Code and 5(2) of Act II of 1947 were pending on 15-10-75 before the Court of Senior Special Judge, Tangail against Fazlul Huq and others for misappropriation of large quantity of cotton yarn, when the Government by a notification of that date transferred the said cases along with others to Special Martial Law Court No. 11 under the Provision of regulation 3(2) of Martial Law Regulation No. 1 of 1975. 

 3. Dr. Razee submits that a Special Judge appointed under Act XL of 1958 is not a Criminal Court within the meaning of the said regulation, as there is no mention of the words conveying the import of such a judge in the regulation. He further says that a Special Judge does not come within any of the categories of Criminal Court mentioned in S. 6 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. None of the contentions is sustainable. The provision of regulation 3(2) may be set out: 

 "The Government may transfer a case from one Martial Law Court or from a Criminal Court of Special Tribunal to a Martial Law Court. 

 4. Section 6(1) of the Act XL of 1958 in clear language says that the Court of a Special Judge shall be deemed to be a Court of Sessions trying cases without the aid of assessors or jury, and that the provisions of the Code of Criminal procedure, except Chapter XXXVIII shall apply to the proceedings of a Court of Special Judge. The Act in unambiguous language confers on the Court of a Special Judge, the status of a Court of Sessions. Furthermore except a minor chapter whole of the Criminal Procedure Code applies to proceedings of such a court. The court of a Special Judge is in terms of the said Act a Criminal Court with the power and status of a Court of Sessions.
